originality.rationale: The new statement is uniform in n and r and includes a refined bivariate polynomial, a total type formula and strictly decreasing algebraic growth bases. Earlier work covers the ideal/filter correspondence, crown order ideals, a fixed 3-neighbor specialization and general algorithms, but these do not entail the explicit all-r bivariate law without a new cyclic-span argument. Partial access to some older generalized-crown ideal-count work and possible unindexed equivalent formulas are genuine residual risks.

The 1974 generalized-crown paper was inspected by abstract only; an equivalent full biclique formula in appendix cannot be conclusively excluded.
The 2005 garland paper was inspected in part but not every page due intermittent PDF access.
Unindexed or different-terminology literature may independently state the exact cyclic biclique polynomial or full random-poset type formula.
